text:
SASRec adds learned absolute position embeddings and uses causal attention; deletion can therefore change content, positions, and the prediction anchor simultaneously. Recommended diagnostic design, inferred from the [original implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py): compare equal-count recent versus older deletions on identical eligible examples. Compacted deletion right-aligns survivors, shifting some position IDs and shortening history. Position-preserving deletion keeps survivors at their original slots and explicitly masks deleted keys/values throughout every layer; zeroing item embeddings alone is insufficient. Both remove information, but their difference reveals sensitivity to packing and positions. Keep the latest item/query fixed for the cleanest comparison; deleting it also changes the prediction anchor. Report this separately, stratify by original length, and exclude empty histories.

Latest-item-fixed shuffling should permute only earlier observed items among occupied slots, preserving padding, item multiset, length, and the latest item’s position. Repeat permutations with fixed seeds. This measures sensitivity to item-position assignments, not a causal effect of real-world order. Freeze targets, candidate IDs, and seen-item exclusions across perturbations; deleted observations must not become newly eligible recommendations. Temporal research shows that unavailable future items can distort evaluation ([Ji et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11060)). Keep the pinned benchmark unchanged; any availability diagnostic should be separate and use public timestamps only, acknowledging that first observation is merely a proxy for availability.

For per-position next-item probes, construct each prefix independently: input x₁…xₜ, target xₜ₊₁, then perturb only that prefix. Shuffling an entire training row before reading intermediate states can move future items across the causal boundary. Preserve the original target and negatives, exclude padding targets, and score the last retained prefix state—not an unchanged tensor index after compaction. This follows the shifted input/positive alignment in the [SASRec sampler](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/sampler.py).
